output:
To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT - Brian: Embakasi casuals, Monday 30 November

Brian,

Read this through on Sunday and keep the checklist with you on Monday. The short version is that this was our failure, not the casuals’. They did the work and have every right to be angry. Do not go in defensive, and do not give them another time we cannot keep.

What actually happened

On Friday, the bank rejected the casuals’ bulk payment file, TLL-CAS-2611B, at validation. The bank had changed its template during its 25 November upgrade, and the beneficiary-reference column in our file exceeded its new character limit. No payments in that file were processed.

The rejection alert went to the old finance mailbox. Kevin only saw it after 5pm, by which time the bank cut-off had passed. That is why there was no payment on Friday. Do not hide behind the bank: the template problem triggered it, but we failed to catch the rejection in time.

Njeri has now approved moving the affected payments to M-Pesa bulk. Kevin’s realistic estimate is money on phones by 11am on Monday. He will not commit to anything earlier.

Peninah has checked the list: 198 numbers are confirmed and 14 remain unreachable, mostly new loaders from the Athi River intake. She will be at Embakasi from 7:30 with the printed list so those 14 can correct their details face to face. She will also have her laptop for anyone who wants a printed payslip.

What you can say to the group

Something along these lines, in your own voice:

“Good morning. I am sorry. Your pay did not arrive on Friday, and that was management’s failure, not yours. You did the work, and you were entitled to be paid without having to chase us.

“The bank rejected our payment file because one field did not meet its new format. The alert went to an old finance mailbox and was seen after the bank cut-off, so no payments in that file went out. Management has approved paying you through M-Pesa instead. Finance’s current realistic estimate is that the money will be on phones by 11am today. I will not give you an earlier time or pretend that I can control the exact minute each phone receives it.

“Everyone on the affected list will also receive KES 500 for today’s lunch and fare in the same approved payment batch. M-Pesa charges are for the company, not for any of you, and nothing is to be deducted from your pay to cover them.

“Peninah will be here from 7:30 with the list. If your number has changed or you are among those we could not reach, please see her. She will also print payslips for anyone who wants one.

“We will give you confirmed progress updates at 8:30 and 10:00, or sooner if anything material changes. If there is a problem, I will tell you plainly rather than disappear and leave you hearing rumours. Again, I am sorry.”

Acknowledge the practical consequences. Joseph says some people have rent due on the 1st. You do not need to wait for them to explain why late pay matters.

What you can promise

- An in-person apology from management, delivered by you on Njeri’s instruction.
- Payment through the approved M-Pesa route, with Finance’s current estimate being Monday by 11am.
- The full pay due to each person on the affected list.
- KES 500 per affected casual for Monday lunch and fare, in the same M-Pesa batch.
- M-Pesa charges borne by the company, not deducted from anyone.
- Peninah at Embakasi from 7:30 with the list, corrections for the 14 unreachable people, and printed payslips on request.
- Fixed, honest updates at 8:30 and 10:00, including an update if the position has not changed.
- That no one will be dismissed or threatened with dismissal on the day. Also, no threats about contracts on Monday.

What you must not promise or do

- Do not say “by breakfast”, “before 9”, “before the trucks leave”, “immediately”, “by lunch” or anything earlier than 11am. Mombasa 2024 is my warning: the supervisor said “by lunch”, money arrived at 4pm, and half the shift sat down. Never again give a time we cannot keep.
- Do not turn the 11am estimate into a guarantee that every individual phone will be credited at the same moment. In particular, the 14 people whose numbers are still unconfirmed must see Peninah first; do not guess or pretend their details are resolved.
- Do not say people have been paid until Finance confirms release, and do not ask someone to accept a screenshot or verbal assurance as though money has arrived.
- Do not offer compensation beyond the approved KES 500, or make the pay or the KES 500 conditional on loading.
- Do not blame the casuals, Joseph, Peninah or Ouma. Do not tell them simply to “be patient” without giving new, verifiable information.
- Do not discuss wider company finances or speculate about why Finance chose a particular arrangement. Keep the explanation to this payment file and the approved payment plan.

Ouma and the Kisumu trucks

Speak to Ouma privately before addressing the whole group, with Joseph present if that helps. Ouma is loud, but he is not a bad man. He has four kids and rent to worry about. Do not wait until he is addressing a crowd and then try to win the argument.

Tell him you wanted to hear him directly, acknowledge that the delay is ours, and ask what the group is saying and what they need clarified. Listen without interrupting. You can ask for his help in keeping the discussion calm, but do not ask him to silence the others and do not single him out publicly as the problem.

If his group still refuses to load:

1. Keep the discussion respectful and move it away from a shouting crowd. Ask Ouma and a small number of representatives to speak with you and Joseph while Peninah handles number verification.
2. Restate the confirmed payment position and update times. Ask whether they will proceed on that basis, but do not bargain with money, invent an earlier time or make loading a condition of receiving what is already owed.
3. Treat an actual stoppage under the joint Operations/HR procedure. It is not an Operations-only decision. Contact me immediately if I am still reachable; if I am airborne or unavailable, escalate to Njeri for management direction and named HR involvement. Do not make Peninah carry that decision simply because she is present.
4. No dismissal, threat of dismissal or contract threats on Monday. Record what happened and what was said, without turning the notes into a retaliation list.
5. Watch the clock. The Kisumu trucks must leave by 9am or we miss the mill’s offloading slot. Do not wait until 8:55 to escalate. If loading is genuinely stopped, escalate immediately and, if unresolved, again by 8:00 so Operations has time to address the departure and mill-slot consequences. That operational planning must not become another threat to the men.

For separate grievances, the normal route remains the shift supervisor first, then HR within 48 hours. A stoppage is not a grievance channel, but never use that sentence to avoid answering the pay complaint itself.

Monday checklist

- 5:30: You at the depot. Speak to Joseph, establish the mood, and check for any confirmed payment update before addressing everyone.
- Before the group gathers: Private conversation with Ouma.
- Before 7:05: WhatsApp me if anything changes. I am up from 4:30 and will read it before boarding.
- 7:30: Peninah on site with the list and laptop.
- 8:00: Hard escalation point if loading remains stopped.
- 8:30 and 10:00: Updates to the group.
- 9:00: Kisumu trucks’ latest departure.
- By 11:00: Finance’s current realistic estimate for M-Pesa credit, subject to confirmed release and correct recipient details.

You are not going there to defend the indefensible. Apologise, give them the facts, and keep every promise you make.
